sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Financial Times, citing two people involved in unofficial efforts to end the war] Putin views the transfer of the unoccupied part of Donbas to Russia merely as a precondition for a ceasefire; as part of a final peace agreement Moscow hopes to secure further territorial concessions, incl. more territory in exchange for any NATO security guarantees. [ATTRIBUTED QUOTE -- via FT sources, NOT a direct Putin quote] 'I will destroy all your infrastructure until you agree. By next year, Ukraine will have no infrastructure left. All bridges, ports, railways, energy infrastructure and power plants will be destroyed.' [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- FT sources] Putin is capitalising on Trump's desire to end the war quickly; the sources consider a ceasefire at the Abu Dhabi talks (Nov 10-11) unlikely. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- BBC, via Panorama] Putin offered to halt his offensive and freeze the front line if Zelenskyy hands over control of eastern Donetsk. [CONTEXT -- Pollar morning brief Nov 7] Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev privately at the White House on Thursday evening; Jared Kushner later wrote Washington is working on security guarantees for Ukraine and a wider European security architecture.
sections.what_verified: 2 distinct declared-tier publisher families: Financial Times (T2) + BBC (T2, via Panorama citing BBC's own reporting). Censor.net, UA.news, United24, RMF24, Mezha and Pollar all carry the FT story and therefore count as the FT family, not independent corroboration; they have no declared tier in the registry in any case.
sections.what_disputed: Strongest counterpoint: FT's own sources say the Abu Dhabi talks are unlikely to produce a ceasefire, and Kaja Kallas (EU foreign policy chief) answered 'Putin does not have a veto over European security'; Zelenskyy has separately said Russian security concerns could be part of a peace agreement and opened the door to online voting for front-line soldiers. The White House line (via Kushner) is that practical arrangements on security guarantees and a wider European security architecture are being worked on -- i.e. Washington is negotiating past the territorial precondition, not accepting it. No Kremlin statement confirms the demand as stated.
sections.why_matters: Proven set: NATO/Russia war warnings + revelations. Hard counted number + warning frame: the Donbas demand as the price of a ceasefire, 3 days before Abu Dhabi. The 'destroy all your infrastructure' line is the hook -- attributed, never presented as a direct Putin quote. Claim-busting frame: FT sources say no ceasefire is likely in Abu Dhabi despite Trump's 'landmark deal' framing.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (FT reported Nov 6; Censor.net Nov 6 20:22 UTC; UA.news Nov 6 21:34 UTC; United24 Nov 6 16:54; zero 'Donbas precondition'/'unoccupied parts of Donbas' mentions in Nov 6 OR Nov 7 scans -- grep confirms) -- Financial Times: Putin demands Ukraine hand over the unoccupied part of Donbas as a precondition for any ceasefire, expects further territorial concessions in a final deal, and threatens to destroy all of Ukraine's infrastructure this winter

The 'destroy all your infrastructure' line is the hook -- attributed, never presented as a direct Putin quote. Claim-busting frame: FT sources say no ceasefire is likely in Abu Dhabi despite Trump's 'landmark deal' framing. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Land for a ceasefire, or fight on?
